original_value: The concept of the technological singularity is frequently reified. Futurist forecasts inferred from this imprecise reification are then criticized, and the reified ideas are incorporated in the core concept. In this paper, I try to disentangle the facts related to the technological singularity from more speculative beliefs about the possibility of creating artificial general intelligence. I use the theory of metasystem transitions and the concept of universal evolution to analyze some misconceptions about the technological singularity. While it may be neither purely technological, nor truly singular, we can predict that the next transition will take place, and that the emerged metasystem will demonstrate exponential growth in complexity with a doubling time of less than half a year, exceeding the complexity of the existing cybernetic systems in few decades.

result.paraphrase: The technological singularity is often treated as a concrete thing. Futurist predictions derived from that vague reification are then criticized, and the reified notions become part of the core concept. In this paper, I seek to separate the facts associated with the technological singularity from more speculative beliefs about the possibility of building artificial general intelligence. Drawing on the theory of metasystem transitions and the notion of universal evolution, I examine several misconceptions about the technological singularity. Although it may be neither purely technological nor truly singular, the next transition can be predicted to occur, and the resulting metasystem will show exponential increases in complexity with a doubling time of under half a year, surpassing the complexity of existing cybernetic systems within a few decades.
